targets.authors: Buchholz M., Gollwitzer M., Magraw-Mickelson Z., Stolz C., Süssenbach P.
targets.title: Taking back control: Findings on the cognitive, behavioral, and motivational consequences of victim sensitivity.
targets.evidence_quote: In light of these limitations, we aimed to replicate their findings using the original and another control compensation strategy, with higher sample sizes in the conditions of interest, to reach sufficient power to detect the expected effect.
targets.outcome_quote: In two studies, we attempted to replicate the finding that providing victim-sensitive individuals with a personal (or structural) sense of control may attenuate the negative effect of victim sensitivity—a latent disposition to fear and avoid exploitation by others—on people’s willingness to trust a partner in a standardized trust game (【19†Buchholz et al., 2023】). However, unlike 【19†Buchholz et al. (2023)】, we were unable to find such an effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall verdict is failure to replicate the central control affirmation effect across both studies. Manipulation limitations are discussed as a possible explanation, not as a definitive verdict that the attempt cannot adjudicate.

reasoning: Two new samples test the published Buchholz et al. finding. Other cited work supplies theory or procedures rather than independently targeted findings. Publisher title and authors match.
